question: Women still make up just 22 % of the EU’s transport workforce, compared to around 46 % across all sectors. The sector remains male-dominated, with strong horizontal and vertical professional stratification. Women are mainly concentrated in management and customer service positions, and are under-represented in technical, operational and leadership functions.

According to a new survey by the European Transport Workers’ Federation (ETF) looking at violence and harassment of women in transport, three in four female workers (74 %) have experienced some form of violence or harassment in the workplace1.

Given that a number of studies have confirmed that the increased participation of women in quality jobs and leadership roles enhances innovation, improves the efficiency of organisations and contributes positively to growth, will the Commission say: 1.

Does it intend to include in the post-2025 gender equality strategy2 a specific objective and a package of actions to strengthen women’s participation in the transport sector, eliminate pay inequalities and improve working conditions?

Does it intend to propose binding minimum standards for safe workplaces, adequate staff training, effective reporting and monitoring mechanisms, and targeted awarenessraising campaigns to make the transport sector attractive and safe for women?
How does it intend to build on, strengthen and monitor the implementation of the 25 recommendations of ‘Women in transport – EU platform for change’ by Member States, businesses and social partners?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.3.2026) The Commission is committed to promoting gender equality and improving working conditions across all sectors, including transport. More women in transport professions will help address labour shortages and strengthen the sector’s performance and competitiveness. 1.

The post-2025 gender equality strategy will highlight ongoing initiatives such as the Women in Transport - EU Platform for Change (WiT) and the network of Ambassadors for #DiversityInTransport which raise awareness and enable exchange of good practices.

The Commission will work with Member States to monitor the implementation of the Pay Transparency Directive1 and with the transport industry to promote better working conditions. 2. In the EU, legislation exists in the field of occupational safety and health (OSH). Council Directive 89/391/EEC2 applies to all sectors, including transport, and to all workers3, including women.

It covers all risks to workers’ health and safety and lays down key principles to prevent and protect against these risks. The current EU Strategic Framework on Health and Safety at Work 2021-2027 includes gender considerations4, and the European Agency for Safety and Health at Work researches and raises awareness of OSH issues for women at work5. 3.

Building on the 25 recommendations6 by the WiT platform, the Commission will continue to collaborate with Member States and social partners in the transport sector to ensure the monitoring and implementation of initiatives to increase women’s participation in transport. Sharing good practices and collecting data will help speed up progress.
1 Directive (EU) 2023/970 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May 2023 to strengthen the

application of the principle of equal pay for equal work or work of equal value between men and women through pay transparency and enforcement mechanisms. 2 Council Directive 89/391/EEC of 12 June 1989 on the introduction of measures to encourage improvements in the safety and health of workers at work (OJ L 183, 29.6.1989, p. 1) - https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/ALL/?uri=celex%3A31989L0391.

3 Within the meaning of Article 3 of the Council Directive 89/391/EEC. 4 Commission Communication on EU strategic framework on health and safety at work 2021-2027 Occupational safety and health in a changing world of work - COM(2021) 323 final. 5 https://osha.europa.eu/en/themes/women-and-health-work. 6 https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/87d21922-35f8-11f0-8a44-01aa75ed71a1/language-en.
